title: Deioces
summary: First king of the Medes in Herodotus (1.96–102); CFAH-5 AP-32 dates him 710/709 BC.
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

standby.note: Standby placement only, placed with "Deioces rules the Medes" (a linked event of this person's life). The year is that record's sort year, taken as-is. No reign length or age was added or subtracted. It is not a sort year.

birth.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

reign.date: “Having reigned three-and-fifty years, Deioces was at his death succeeded by his son Phraortes.”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.102 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 47 (PDF p. 49)
reign.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): CFAH AP-32 (710/709 BC) − 53 = 657/656 BC for the death of Deioces. Generations (2nd ed.) prints Deioces 712–675 BC (37 years); Herodotus gives 53.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 789a
reign.note: Year cell "3999 3317 324". The third printed figure 324 is the column "Temple", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 53 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row.
